necessary_context.content: Definition 3.1 places the unknown minimizer within distance r of the origin and restricts queries to distance 1000r. Definition 3.2 returns noisy function value and tangent gradient, with noise terms independent across different queries; independence between value and gradient noise is not asserted. Definition 3.3 bounds the noise density by c and noise magnitude by C. The footnote explains why removing the query-radius restriction changes the information model.
necessary_context.name: Radius-r noisy gradient model

necessary_context.applies_to: Theorem 4.3; this context does not resolve its parameter-boundary or resource ambiguities
necessary_context.content: Definition 4.2 chooses the hidden index uniformly from {1,...,n}. A query q in Q yields an observation in X sampled from density f_(q,i*). Success means guessing the hidden index with probability at least 2/3. X is a Euclidean observation region and |X| denotes its volume. Theorem 4.3 states a query lower bound of order log(n)/log(c|X|) under the common density cap c.
necessary_context.name: Noisy query game

necessary_context.applies_to: Source interpretation of the noisy-query argument
necessary_context.content: Section 4.2 augments each observation by a vertical coordinate sampled uniformly under its density graph. Uniform prior and unit graph volumes give a uniform posterior on surviving indices. Lemma 4.4 bounds the expected reduction of log survivor count by log(c|X|), using the integral of N log N and Jensen's inequality. The displayed proof of Theorem 4.3 then uses cumulative progress and Markov's inequality. This is a source proof map, not a local replacement proof.
necessary_context.locator: PDF pp.7–8, Section 4.2, Lemma 4.4 and Proof of Theorem 4.3
necessary_context.name: Transparent-game proof map

necessary_context.applies_to: Selected squared-distance construction and its noisy-query reduction
necessary_context.content: Comment 1 describes exponentially many centers on the radius-r hyperbolic circle, pairwise separated by at least r/2, with objective dist(x,x*)^2. The optimization interface has bounded-radius queries and noisy value/gradient feedback. The proof on p.8 reduces r/5 localization to identifying the center and bounds the answer region using a value interval and a Euclidean tangent-gradient disk. Section 4 states that an exact gradient recovers the center in one query; this construction therefore supplies no exact-gradient lower bound.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.5, Section 4; p.6, Comment 1; p.8, Proof of Theorem 4.1
necessary_context.name: Packing reduction and escape limits

source_issues.issue: The proof uses n_T=1 when the player determines the hidden index. Definition 4.2 allows a guess with success probability 2/3; this does not directly require a singleton posterior on every successful run. The bridge requires an explicit argument. No repair is claimed here.

The statement does not explicitly distinguish fixed query budget from expected stopping time; surrounding prose mentions expectation while the displayed proof uses T without supplying a stopping-time argument. Degenerate c|X|=1 and small-n regimes are not explicitly resolved.
source_issues.locator: PDF pp.6–8, Theorem 4.3 and its proof

source_issues.issue: The squared-distance Hessian normalization and the continuation's answer-volume estimate O(r^4 C^3) require calibration, especially for small C. The cited external Hessian source has not been checked. No unrestricted or exact-oracle lower bound is extracted.
source_issues.locator: PDF p.8, Proof of Theorem 4.1; text continuation p.9
